title: I, As a Constellation
statement: “I” is a plural self: a body drawn from memory, a map of where I have been, an inward-looking aperture, a bridge toward others, and a red current of feeling that keeps moving.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.error: Use a boolean done and at most 12 actions; an empty batch is allowed only when done is true or reviewOnly is true.

notes.note: Build the central self as a layered, inhabited figure: mapped ground, drawn body, inner oculus, bridge of relation, and vivid current of feeling. This first pass prioritizes a clear vertical composition with ample breathing room.

actions.title: I, As a Constellation
actions.statement: “I” is a plural self: a body drawn from memory, a map of where I have been, an inward-looking aperture, a bridge toward others, and a red current of feeling that keeps moving.

notes.note: The initial image is coherent but overly rectilinear. Add an ornamental vertical weave behind the figure and two organic presences at the lower edges, so the self reads less as a diagram and more as an ecology of memory, body, and relation.
Clarify the self-portrait’s hierarchy: let the drawn body emerge in front of the bridge, remove the accidental small paper wedge, and add a clockwork core as the interior labor of saying “I.”

The observed collage has a strong altar-like vertical form, but the tiny shell fragment and white gear cut interrupt its clarity. Remove those distractions and introduce a precisely cropped green beetle as a small, alert witness beside the figure.
notes.error: This cut overlaps material already used by beetle-witness.

notes.note: Refine the observed composition by clearing the two small interruptions on the figure, then reactivate the already-cut jewel beetle as a bright, watchful counterpoint near the bridge.

The composition’s central figure and surrounding ecology are now legible. Remove the small beetle cut, whose pale rectangular field distracts from the bridge and interrupts the otherwise deliberate balance of the layered self-portrait.

The current canvas resolves most strongly as an emblematic, layered self-portrait: map, textile, oculus, bridge, drawn body, and red current. Remove the two lower organic cutouts, whose pale source-paper margins read as unintended wedges and weaken the otherwise clean silhouette.

The central figure, oculus, bridge, and map now form a clear symbolic “I.” Refine the red current so it reads as the fish itself rather than as a large pale geometric banner crossing the figure’s feet.

The fish’s remaining cream source field reads as a conspicuous horizontal wedge beneath the figure rather than as an integrated current. Remove it to preserve the cleaner altar-like self-portrait made by the map, textile, eye, bridge, and body.

The finished collage is a clear image of “I” as a situated, relational self: an inward eye above a drawn body, held between map, pattern, and bridge. The existing title and statement remain present and complete.
